items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its MA stack, then overlay the option-flow call fraction and put-versus-call premium to judge whether an index holding near highs is being carried by a narrowing set of leaders.
items.note: A narrow-leadership divergence has opened this window. SPY closed 772.67, just 0.67% under its 52-week high in a bull-stacked MA regime (50-day distance +3.17%, 200-day +9.88%), yet only 26.1% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 33.9-point shortfall to the 60% broad-participation threshold and a sharp step down from the roughly half-positive breadth of the prior window. At the same time option flow has flipped to put-heavy: calls are just 36.95% of premium, with $1.29B of call premium against $2.20B of puts across 12 tickers and 1670 flagged contracts. VIX 15.19 keeps this in the pressure-not-panic band, but a headline index pinned near highs on 26% breadth while hedging demand rises is the classic thinning-leadership pattern, where the average stock is already rolling over beneath a firm index. This is what to watch: whether breadth re-broadens or the index converges down to a weakening tape.
items.title: Index holds near its 52-week high while breadth collapses to 26% and flow turns put-heavy

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative; signedNetGEX=-2.51B; flip=775.96; callWall=773; putWall=772; expectedMove=2.79; spot=772.61

items.method: Read the options-structure signed net-gamma sign and its flip and wall levels against current spot, confirm the dealer scenario and hold from the gamma playbook, then overlay the most-unusual option prints and the intraday VWAP to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price have converged on the downside edge of the gamma structure. Signed net gamma is negative at about -$2.51B, and SPY spot 772.61 has dropped below the 775.96 flip and now rests right on the 772 put wall, with the 773 call wall barely overhead and a front expected move of only plus or minus 2.79 — an unusually tight 772/773 band. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so pressure at a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape agrees: the single most unusual print in the feed is a same-day SPY 775 put at $209.9M on 75.9x open interest — the largest premium on the board — and overall flow is put-heavy. The live auction is a trend-day-down under mixed control with VWAP 774.1 sitting above spot. This is a coiled range-break-watch structure: while 772 holds, the tight band and low VIX 15.19 keep it orderly, but the compressed walls plus short-gamma hedging mean a sustained loss of the 772 put wall is the level that would tip the balance toward acceleration rather than fade.
items.title: SPY spot has slipped below the negative-gamma flip and is sitting on the 772 put wall under a record same-day put print
